Guidance & outlook: India's Logistics Market was valued at USD 228.4 Billion in 2024 and is expected to reach USD 428.7 Billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 6.50%.

According to the reports published by Statistics The logistics cost of Third-Party Logistics (3PL) market is expected to amount to US $0.54 Trillion in 2027, potentially depicting how much the 3PL market can grow almost $6 Billion in the fiscal year 2025.
On a consolidated basis, OBCL recorded revenue from operations of ₹347.21 crore during FY 2025-26, compared with ₹338.85 crore in the previous financial year.
Growth & demand: The market size of the Indian logistics market would grow to USD 563 Billion dollars in 2030, at a compound annual growth rate 9.4 percent.
LOOKING AHEAD As we enter the next phase of our journey, our focus is not merely on growth in scale, but on creating quality and sustainable growth.

According to industry estimates, the Indian logistics market was valued at approximately USD 243.8 billion in 2025 and is expected to witness sustained growth in the coming years, reinforcing its strategic role in India's economic development.
Margins & costs: 30,987.71 Lakhs at an operating margin of approximately 6% The financial year 2025-26 unfolded against a backdrop of continued global uncertainty and economic shifts.

The provisions relating to the maintenance of cost records under Section 148(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014 are not applicable to the Company.
India's logistics costs are estimated to remain at approximately 13-14% of GDP, higher than the 8-10% observed in many developed economies.
Capex & expansion: Our priorities for the years ahead will remain centred on customer centricity, operational excellence, prudent financial management, technology adoption and sustainable expansion.
DOWNSTREAM INVESTMENT The Company neither have any Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) nor invested as any Downstream Investment in any other Company in India .
Further, there were no acts of omission/commission by the Company itself, leading to the disqualification of its directors.
Balance sheet & cash: Our Company effectively manages its working capital through a streamlined process, ensuring constant oversight and control over receivables, payables and other key factors.
In view of growth plans, your directors do not recommend any dividend for the Financial Year under review.
SEBI under Regulation 43A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 requires top 1000 listed companies based on market capitalization to formulate a Dividend Distribution Policy.
Risks & challenges: The common risks inherent are: Regulations, Competition, business risk, technology obsolescence, long term investments and expansion of facilities.
Business risk, inter alia, includes financial risk, political risk, legal risk etc., As a part of the plan, these risks are assessed and steps as appropriate are taken to mitigate the same.
However, growth prospects remain subject to risks arising from geopolitical conflicts, evolving trade policies, fiscal uncertainties, and financial market volatility.
